headline: Genetic effects on gene regulation mapped at cell-type and single-molecule resolution
label: Single Cell Regulatory Genetics
summary: Single-cell eQTL mixed models, uncertainty-aware cell-type TWAS and single-molecule accessibility prediction push variant interpretation beyond bulk tracks.
synthesis: The dominant thread is linking genetic variation to regulatory readouts at cell-type or single-molecule resolution rather than in bulk. SAIGE-QTL fits a Poisson mixed model to single-cell read counts, reporting better-calibrated and more scalable eQTL mapping than pseudobulk approaches, including trans effects. ATTICUS transfers bulk-pretrained personalised sequence representations to cell-type TWAS and adds uncertainty-aware expression prediction. Mola, within the S2d sequence-to-distribution framework, predicts single-molecule chromatin accessibility distributions from DNA sequence. An XGBoost-SHAP model on snATAC-seq from iPSC-derived pancreatic progenitors prioritizes lower-frequency noncoding variants predicted to disrupt HNF4A motifs, outperforming linear models. A second, looser thread is multimodal integration: COATI couples scRNA and scATAC trajectories via unbalanced synchronized optimal transport, scHiR jointly embeds scRNA-seq and scHi-C, and CloneVI relates mitochondrial clones to cell state. Sample-level embedding, TCR-phenotype inference and composition benchmarking are adjacent rather than variant-focused.
